ai.title: Add gpt4o fallback for unmatched search/replace blocks
ai.summary: The backend now invokes `applyRemainingChanges` using `gpt4o` when search/replace blocks fail to match after retry logic. `processFileBlock` captures blocks that don't match and passes them to the new fallback mechanism to ensure all intended changes are applied. This internal update in `backend/src/process-file-block.ts` and `backend/src/generate-diffs-prompt.ts` improves robustness for complex file edits.

eli5.text: When the system edits a file and a piece of an edit doesn't quite line up with the existing text after a few retries, it now switches to a different AI model to make sure that piece gets applied instead of being skipped. This only affects the internal editing workflow and doesn't change what features are available today.

ai.title: Fix quota display and overage fees for subscribers
ai.summary: QuotaManager now returns `subscription_active` flag alongside usage data. Backend propagates this state via `usage-response` websocket messages to client. CLI `showUsageWarning` logic updated to distinguish between blocked non-subscribers and warned subscribers. Paid quota limit reduced from 50M to 10M credits in `constants.ts`.

eli5.text: When you run out of quota, the app now shows different messages depending on whether you're a paying subscriber or not. Subscribers see a warning about potential overage fees, while non-subscribers are blocked from using the service. The system now tracks and displays your subscription status alongside your usage data, so the app can tell the difference between someone who should be blocked and someone who should just be warned. Paying subscribers also now have a lower quota limit of 10 million credits instead of 50 million, and overage charges have been raised to 95 cents per 100 credits.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.95
ai.summary: Version bumped from 1.0.94 to 1.0.95 in `npm-app/package.json`. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: Updating to this version lets the assistant now automatically try a newer AI model when its first attempt to apply your code edits misses the mark, so edits that previously failed will now often succeed on a second try. It also fixes the pricing page so subscribers see their quota usage and any extra charges correctly, adds a link to cancel your paid subscription through Stripe, and stops the page from being embedded by other sites. If you install this update, you'll notice failed edits retry themselves in the background, your billing page showing the right numbers, and the pricing card lining up properly.

ai.title: Pro overage charge raised to $0.95 per 100 credits
ai.summary: Pro overage cost raised to $0.95 per 100 credits, up from $0.90. Change applied to pricing page features array in web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx. Only web pricing surface affected; no core constants or CLI picker changes. Follow-up constraint: verify billing engine matches displayed rate.

eli5.text: If you have the Pro plan and go past your monthly credit limit, each extra 100 credits now costs $0.95 instead of $0.90. This only shows up on the pricing page you read when deciding to upgrade; the actual billing system still needs to be checked to make sure it charges the new rate. You’d notice the price listed under the Pro plan’s features changed by five cents per 100 credits.

ai.title: Stripe webhook handles subscription updates and cancellations
ai.summary: The Stripe webhook handler now processes `customer.subscription.updated` events and clears `stripe_price_id` when `cancellation_details.reason` is present. `stripe_price_id` is exposed in NextAuth sessions and types, enabling the pricing page to display conditional renewal or cancellation links. Checkout sessions now allow promotion codes.

eli5.text: When your paid subscription gets canceled, the site now correctly stops treating you as an active subscriber and clears your pricing info. You would notice that the pricing page shows different messages depending on your subscription status: either a "Need to cancel? Click here" link if you still have an active paid plan, or a "Your subscription won't renew" message if your subscription was canceled. The checkout screen you use to upgrade also now accepts promo codes if you have one. This is all live today.

ai.title: Clickjacking fix via X-Frame-Options header
ai.summary: Added `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` to `web/next.config.mjs` headers. Prevents clickjacking by restricting frame embedding to same origin. Scope limited to web config.

eli5.text: The web application now sends a small security instruction that stops other websites from embedding it inside a hidden frame, which is a common trick used to trick people into clicking things they can't see. This protection applies to every page of the web app and is active right now. If you're an internal user viewing the site, everything looks the same, but outside sites can no longer disguise parts of it in invisible boxes.

ai.title: Fix installer console.log in update-manicode
ai.summary: update-manicode.ts renamed installer var to installerInfo to match detectInstaller object return. Updated console.log to use installerInfo.installer. Passed installerInfo to runUpdateManicode. Changed goodbye message to 'Manicode out!'.
